subject: Maths
title: Sine and cosine rules
subtitle: Trigonometry · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can apply the sine rule and cosine rule to find unknown sides and angles in non-right-angled triangles.

key_vocab.definition: The sine rule is used when you have a side and its opposite angle: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C. The cosine rule is used when you know two sides and the included angle (or all three sides).

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can apply the sine rule and cosine rule to find unknown sides and angles in non-right-angled triangles.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: sine rule -- The sine rule is used when you have a side and its opposite angle: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C. The cosine rule is used when you know two sides and the included angle (or all three sides).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Sine rule for matched pairs (side + opposite angle). Cosine rule for SAS or SSS.
&frac{a}{sin A} = &frac{b}{sin B}
Each side is proportional to the sine of its opposite angle

Key examples:
  ✓ Sine rule: a/sin A = b/sin B  (for matching pairs of side and angle)
  ✓ Cosine rule: a² = b² + c² - 2bc cos A  (SAS or SSS)
  ✓ Use sine rule for AAS or ASA  (when you can match a pair)
  ✗ Sine rule works with two sides and included angle  (use cosine rule for SAS)
  ✗ a² = b² + c² + 2bc cos A  (sign should be minus)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – sine rule finding a side
  In triangle ABC, A = 40°, B = 70°, a = 8. Find b.
  a/sin A = b/sin B
  8/sin 40° = b/sin 70°
  b = 8 sin 70° / sin 40° = 11.7 (1 dp)
  b = 11.7
  (Cross-multiply to find the unknown side.)

Example 2 – sine rule finding an angle
  In triangle, a = 10, b = 7, A = 50°. Find B.
  sin B / b = sin A / a
  sin B = 7 sin 50° / 10 = 0.536
  B = sin⁻¹(0.536) = 32.4°
  B = 32.4°
  (Use the sine rule flipped to find the angle.)

sections.title: Sine rule - finding sides
sections.content:
Use the sine rule to find the unknown side (1 dp).

(a) A = 50°, B = 60°, a = 10. Find b.
(b) A = 30°, C = 80°, a = 6. Find c.
(c) B = 45°, C = 75°, b = 9. Find c.
(d) A = 40°, B = 55°, b = 12. Find a.

sections.title: Sine rule - finding angles
sections.content:
Use the sine rule to find the unknown angle (1 dp).

(a) a = 8, b = 6, A = 50°. Find B.
(b) a = 12, b = 9, A = 70°. Find B.
(c) b = 10, c = 7, B = 65°. Find C.
(d) a = 15, c = 11, A = 80°. Find C.

sections.title: Cosine rule - finding sides
sections.content:
Use the cosine rule to find the unknown side (1 dp).

(a) b = 7, c = 9, A = 50°. Find a.
(b) a = 6, c = 10, B = 80°. Find b.
(c) a = 5, b = 8, C = 120°. Find c.
(d) b = 4, c = 6, A = 45°. Find a.

sections.title: Cosine rule - finding angles
sections.content:
Use the cosine rule to find the unknown angle (1 dp).

(a) a = 7, b = 5, c = 8. Find A.
(b) a = 10, b = 8, c = 6. Find A.
(c) a = 4, b = 5, c = 6. Find C.
(d) a = 9, b = 7, c = 5. Find A.

sections.title: Mixed problems
sections.content:
Choose and apply the correct rule (1 dp).

(a) A = 35°, B = 85°, a = 7. Find b.
(b) a = 10, b = 12, C = 70°. Find c.
(c) a = 8, b = 9, c = 11. Find largest angle.
(d) B = 40°, b = 8, c = 10. Find C.
(e) a = 5, c = 7, B = 100°. Find b.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ The sine rule uses matching pairs of side and opposite angle
✗ Use the sine rule when you know two sides and the included angle
✓ a² = b² + c² - 2bc cos A is the cosine rule
✗ The cosine rule has a plus sign: a² = b² + c² + 2bc cos A
✓ If cos A is negative, then angle A is obtuse
